//! Closed-form initializers (Phase 1.1): a surface's parameters from a handful
//! of facets, exactly, with no iteration and no seed patch.
//!
//! Phase 1's earned patch grows face by face under validation, which means it
//! must fit a surface to *tiny* support — where a free least-squares fit is
//! hopeless. The sagitta arithmetic: over a 7.5° arc on r = 0.5 the sag is
//! ~0.001 mm against a 2e-5 mm mesh quantum, so a free radius comes out ~2%
//! wrong, about 200× the vertex tolerance. What rescues it is that **facet
//! normals carry exact information**, which turns each surface type into a
//! small linear problem rather than an optimization.
//!
//! Nothing here iterates and nothing here is tuned. Every constant is a
//! numeric-conditioning floor — it decides whether a quantity is *defined*,
//! never whether a fit is *good* — and each is documented as such at its
//! definition.
//!
//! # Which facets to initialize from, and why it matters more than the formula
//!
//! Phase 1.0 measured two things that make facet *selection* part of the
//! algorithm rather than an afterthought (numbers in TODO.md 1.0):
//!
//! 1. **The axis error is `perpendicularity error / |n₁ × n₂|`**, verified to
//!    0.1%. Adjacent facets differ in normal by the exporter's angular step, so
//!    `|n₁ × n₂| ≈ sin(step)` — 0.043 on a fine mesh, a ~23× amplification that
//!    gets *worse* as the mesh refines. So pair the angularly most distant
//!    facets available, never neighbours.
//! 2. **A facet's normal is perpendicular to the axis iff two of its vertices
//!    share a ruling** ([`min_ruling_gap_rad`]). 25.6% of corpus cylinder facets
//!    straddle three or more rulings, and they carry *all* of the
//!    perpendicularity error — aligned facets are exact to 0.0006° worst case
//!    over the whole corpus, straddling ones reach 1.0528°.
//!
//! Both are checkable here without ground truth, so [`select_axis_pair`] does
//! it in two passes: pick the most distant normal pair to get a provisional
//! axis, then re-pick among the facets that are ruling-aligned *with respect to
//! that axis*. The instrument that measured (2) and the code that acts on it
//! call the same function, so they cannot drift apart.

use super::{cross3, dot3, face_centroid, normalize3, perpendicular_basis};
use crate::stage1::{ConnectedMesh, MeshFace, MeshVertex};

/// A closed-form fit, ready to hand to validation and growth.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum Initial {
    Cylinder {
        axis_pos: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
    },
    Sphere {
        centre: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
    },
    Cone {
        apex: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        half_angle: f64,
    },
    Torus {
        centre: [f64; 3],
        axis_dir: [f64; 3],
        major: f64,
        minor: f64,
    },
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Conditioning floors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Below this, two unit normals are parallel to within double-precision noise
/// and their cross product carries no direction at all.
///
/// A validity floor, not a threshold: it decides whether the axis *exists*, not
/// whether it is good enough. The quality of a well-defined axis is governed by
/// the amplification law in the module docs, which is a continuous relation with
/// no cut in it.
const MIN_CROSS_NORM: f64 = 1.0e-9;

/// Below this angular gap (radians) two of a facet's vertices lie on the same
/// ruling.
///
/// Not a tuned threshold: measured over the corpus the two cases are separated
/// by five orders of magnitude of empty space — vertices on one ruling differ
/// only by float32 mesh noise (p50 reads 5.551e-16 rad) while distinct rulings
/// are separated by the exporter's angular step (p95 1.178e-1 rad). Any cut
/// between gives the same answer.
pub(crate) const RULING_SAME_RAD: f64 = 1.0e-6;

/// A null-space direction is only accepted when the next singular value is at
/// least this many times larger, i.e. the null space is one-dimensional.
///
/// A rank test, not a quality threshold. It exists because the torus system is
/// *rank-deficient by construction* on the wrong data: on a sphere every axis
/// through the centre satisfies meridian coplanarity, so the solve has a
/// three-dimensional null space and any answer it returns is arbitrary. This
/// makes the initializer decline rather than invent an axis.
const MIN_RANK_GAP: f64 = 1.0e3;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Facet selection
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The smallest angular gap, in radians, between any two of a facet's vertices
/// measured around the axis `(axis_pos, axis_dir)` — zero exactly when two
/// vertices share a ruling.
///
/// This decides whether a facet normal on a ruled surface is perpendicular to
/// the axis at all. Parametrize the cylinder as
/// `p(θ, z) = a + r(cos θ · u + sin θ · v) + z · d`. The facet's plane contains
/// `d` — equivalently `n ⟂ d` — iff the vertices, projected along `d` onto the
/// plane perpendicular to it, are collinear. They land on a circle of radius
/// `r`, and three points on a circle are collinear only when two of them
/// coincide. **So `n ⟂ d` exactly when two vertices share a ruling**, and a
/// triangle straddling three distinct rulings tilts its normal off perpendicular
/// however perfect the underlying cylinder is.
pub(crate) fn min_ruling_gap_rad(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    fi: usize,
    axis_pos: [f64; 3],
    axis_dir: [f64; 3],
) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut d = axis_dir;
    if normalize3(&mut d) == 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);

    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
    if n < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut thetas = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    for k in 0..n {
        let vtx = &mesh.vertices[face.vertex_indices[k]];
        let w = [
            vtx.x - axis_pos[0],
            vtx.y - axis_pos[1],
            vtx.z - axis_pos[2],
        ];
        let axial = dot3(&w, &d);
        let radial = [
            w[0] - axial * d[0],
            w[1] - axial * d[1],
            w[2] - axial * d[2],
        ];
        thetas.push(dot3(&radial, &v).atan2(dot3(&radial, &u)));
    }

    let mut min_gap = f64::MAX;
    for i in 0..n {
        for j in (i + 1)..n {
            let mut delta = (thetas[i] - thetas[j]).abs();
            if delta > std::f64::consts::PI {
                delta = std::f64::consts::TAU - delta;
            }
            min_gap = min_gap.min(delta);
        }
    }
    Some(min_gap)
}

/// `|n_i × n_j|` — how well-conditioned the pair is as an axis source, and
/// exactly the denominator in the amplification law.
fn pair_conditioning(a: &[f64; 3], b: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    let c = cross3(a, b);
    (c[0] * c[0] + c[1] * c[1] + c[2] * c[2]).sqrt()
}

/// The most angularly distant pair of facet normals in `faces`.
fn widest_normal_pair(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<(usize, usize, f64)> {
    let mut best: Option<(usize, usize, f64)> = None;
    for (a, &fi) in faces.iter().enumerate() {
        let Some(ni) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else {
            continue;
        };
        for &fj in &faces[a + 1..] {
            let Some(nj) = mesh.faces[fj].normal else {
                continue;
            };
            let k = pair_conditioning(&ni, &nj);
            if best.is_none_or(|(_, _, bk)| k > bk) {
                best = Some((fi, fj, k));
            }
        }
    }
    best
}

/// Pick the pair of facets to take an axis from: ruling-aligned, and as
/// angularly distant as the patch allows.
///
/// Two passes, because alignment is defined relative to an axis we do not have
/// yet. The first pass gives a provisional axis good enough to *classify*
/// facets — misjudging alignment needs an axis error of order the angular step,
/// far beyond what pass one produces — and the second pass re-picks among the
/// facets that survive. If too few survive, the provisional pair stands: a
/// worse-conditioned axis is still better than no axis, and validation
/// downstream is what decides whether the fit lives.
///
/// Returns the pair and the axis direction it implies.
fn select_axis_pair(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<(usize, usize, [f64; 3])> {
    let axis_of = |fi: usize, fj: usize| -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
        let (ni, nj) = (mesh.faces[fi].normal?, mesh.faces[fj].normal?);
        let mut axis = cross3(&ni, &nj);
        if normalize3(&mut axis) < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
            return None;
        }
        Some(axis)
    };

    let (pi, pj, _) = widest_normal_pair(faces, mesh)?;
    let provisional = axis_of(pi, pj)?;

    // Any point on the provisional axis will do to measure ruling gaps: the
    // gap is an angle about the axis direction, and shifting the reference
    // point along or across the axis moves every vertex's θ together.
    let anchor = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[pi], &mesh.vertices);
    let aligned: Vec<usize> = faces
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|&fi| {
            min_ruling_gap_rad(mesh, fi, anchor, provisional)
                .is_some_and(|gap| gap < RULING_SAME_RAD)
        })
        .collect();

    if aligned.len() >= 2 {
        if let Some((ai, aj, _)) = widest_normal_pair(&aligned, mesh) {
            if let Some(axis) = axis_of(ai, aj) {
                return Some((ai, aj, axis));
            }
        }
    }
    Some((pi, pj, provisional))
}

/// Every distinct vertex index used by `faces`.
fn patch_vertices(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for &fi in faces {
        let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
        for k in 0..f.vertex_count as usize {
            let vi = f.vertex_indices[k];
            if !out.contains(&vi) {
                out.push(vi);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cylinder
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A cylinder from its facets' normals: axis from `n₁ × n₂`, then radius and
/// position from the existing circle fit in the plane perpendicular to it.
///
/// Exact on a ruling-aligned tessellation at any coarseness — a facet spanning
/// two rulings has its normal exactly perpendicular to the axis, so two such
/// normals span the perpendicular plane and their cross product *is* the axis.
pub(crate) fn cylinder(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<Initial> {
    let (_, _, axis_dir) = select_axis_pair(faces, mesh)?;
    let verts = patch_vertices(faces, mesh);
    let (axis_pos, radius) =
        super::cylindrical::fit_circle_for_axis(&axis_dir, &verts, &mesh.vertices)?;
    Some(Initial::Cylinder {
        axis_pos,
        axis_dir,
        radius,
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sphere
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The circumcenter of a facet's first three vertices.
///
/// For a facet inscribed in a sphere this is the one point of the facet whose
/// normal line passes **exactly** through the centre: the circumcenter is
/// equidistant from three points of the sphere, so it lies on the axis of the
/// circle they define, which is the line through the sphere's centre. The
/// centroid does not have this property, which is why the initializer uses the
/// circumcenter and the diagnostic in `crate::reference` measures against it.
fn circumcenter(face: &MeshFace, vertices: &[MeshVertex]) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
    if (face.vertex_count as usize) < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let p = |k: usize| {
        let v = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[k]];
        [v.x, v.y, v.z]
    };
    let (a, b, c) = (p(0), p(1), p(2));
    let ab = [b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2]];
    let ac = [c[0] - a[0], c[1] - a[1], c[2] - a[2]];
    let n = cross3(&ab, &ac);
    let denom = 2.0 * dot3(&n, &n);
    if denom <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let t1 = cross3(&n, &ab);
    let t2 = cross3(&ac, &n);
    let ac2 = dot3(&ac, &ac);
    let ab2 = dot3(&ab, &ab);
    Some([
        a[0] + (t1[0] * ac2 + t2[0] * ab2) / denom,
        a[1] + (t1[1] * ac2 + t2[1] * ab2) / denom,
        a[2] + (t1[2] * ac2 + t2[2] * ab2) / denom,
    ])
}

/// Midpoint of the common perpendicular between two lines — the standard
/// near-intersection, and the sphere centre when both lines pass through it.
fn common_perpendicular_midpoint(
    p1: [f64; 3],
    d1: [f64; 3],
    p2: [f64; 3],
    d2: [f64; 3],
) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
    let (mut u, mut v) = (d1, d2);
    if normalize3(&mut u) == 0.0 || normalize3(&mut v) == 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    let w = [p1[0] - p2[0], p1[1] - p2[1], p1[2] - p2[2]];
    let b = dot3(&u, &v);
    let denom = 1.0 - b * b;
    if denom < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
        return None;
    }
    let d = dot3(&u, &w);
    let e = dot3(&v, &w);
    let s = (b * e - d) / denom;
    let t = (e - b * d) / denom;
    Some([
        0.5 * ((p1[0] + u[0] * s) + (p2[0] + v[0] * t)),
        0.5 * ((p1[1] + u[1] * s) + (p2[1] + v[1] * t)),
        0.5 * ((p1[2] + u[2] * s) + (p2[2] + v[2] * t)),
    ])
}

/// A sphere from the concurrence of its facets' normal lines.
///
/// Every facet inscribed in a sphere has a normal line through the centre when
/// anchored at its circumcenter, so two facets locate the centre exactly. The
/// pair is chosen by the same conditioning rule as the cylinder — two nearly
/// parallel normal lines meet nowhere useful, which Phase 1.0 measured directly
/// (a pair centre error reaching 4.079 mm at `|n₁ × n₂|` ≈ 0.0436).
///
/// The radius is the mean distance from the centre to the patch's vertices,
/// which uses every facet rather than the two.
pub(crate) fn sphere(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<Initial> {
    let (fi, fj, _) = widest_normal_pair(faces, mesh)?;
    let (ni, nj) = (mesh.faces[fi].normal?, mesh.faces[fj].normal?);
    if pair_conditioning(&ni, &nj) < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
        return None;
    }
    let ci = circumcenter(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)?;
    let cj = circumcenter(&mesh.faces[fj], &mesh.vertices)?;
    let centre = common_perpendicular_midpoint(ci, ni, cj, nj)?;

    let verts = patch_vertices(faces, mesh);
    if verts.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut sum = 0.0;
    for &vi in &verts {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
        let d = [v.x - centre[0], v.y - centre[1], v.z - centre[2]];
        sum += dot3(&d, &d).sqrt();
    }
    let radius = sum / verts.len() as f64;
    if radius <= 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    Some(Initial::Sphere { centre, radius })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// An oblique unit axis: an axis-aligned one would let a sign or an index
    /// slip through every assertion here.
    fn oblique_axis() -> [f64; 3] {
        let mut d = [0.3, -0.5, 0.81];
        normalize3(&mut d);
        d
    }

    /// `|â × b̂|` = sin of the angle between two directions.
    ///
    /// The only well-conditioned way to assert near-parallelism: an angle from
    /// `acos` cannot resolve below ~1e-6° because `acos` amplifies a 1e-16
    /// rounding error into ~1.5e-8 rad. The cross product is linear in the
    /// error and resolves to machine epsilon.
    fn parallel_miss(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
        let (mut u, mut v) = (a, b);
        normalize3(&mut u);
        normalize3(&mut v);
        let c = cross3(&u, &v);
        (c[0] * c[0] + c[1] * c[1] + c[2] * c[2]).sqrt()
    }

    fn vsub(a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
        [a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]]
    }

    fn vnorm(a: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
        dot3(&a, &a).sqrt()
    }

    /// Perpendicular distance from `p` to the line `(pos, dir)`.
    fn distance_to_axis(p: [f64; 3], pos: [f64; 3], dir: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
        let mut d = dir;
        normalize3(&mut d);
        let w = vsub(p, pos);
        let t = dot3(&w, &d);
        vnorm(vsub(w, [d[0] * t, d[1] * t, d[2] * t]))
    }

    /// Build a mesh from explicit faces, computing each facet normal from its
    /// geometry exactly as stage 1 does.
    fn mesh_from(points: Vec<[f64; 3]>, faces: Vec<Vec<usize>>) -> ConnectedMesh {
        let vertices: Vec<MeshVertex> = points
            .iter()
            .map(|p| MeshVertex::from_xyz(p[0], p[1], p[2]))
            .collect();
        let faces = faces
            .into_iter()
            .map(|idx| {
                let p = |k: usize| points[idx[k]];
                let mut n = cross3(&vsub(p(1), p(0)), &vsub(p(2), p(0)));
                normalize3(&mut n);
                let mut vertex_indices = [0usize; 4];
                vertex_indices[..idx.len()].copy_from_slice(&idx);
                MeshFace {
                    vertex_count: idx.len() as u8,
                    vertex_indices,
                    neighbors: [-1; 4],
                    normal: Some(n),
                }
            })
            .collect();
        ConnectedMesh {
            vertices,
            faces,
            stats: Default::default(),
        }
    }

    /// A strip-tessellated cylinder: quads spanning two rulings each, exactly
    /// as a B-rep faceter emits them.
    fn cylinder_strip(
        origin: [f64; 3],
        d: [f64; 3],
        radius: f64,
        steps: usize,
        arc: f64,
    ) -> ConnectedMesh {
        let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);
        let at = |theta: f64, z: f64| {
            [
                origin[0] + radius * (u[0] * theta.cos() + v[0] * theta.sin()) + d[0] * z,
                origin[1] + radius * (u[1] * theta.cos() + v[1] * theta.sin()) + d[1] * z,
                origin[2] + radius * (u[2] * theta.cos() + v[2] * theta.sin()) + d[2] * z,
            ]
        };
        let mut points = Vec::new();
        for k in 0..=steps {
            let theta = arc * k as f64 / steps as f64;
            points.push(at(theta, 0.0));
            points.push(at(theta, 4.0));
        }
        let faces = (0..steps)
            .map(|k| vec![2 * k, 2 * k + 1, 2 * k + 3, 2 * k + 2])
            .collect();
        mesh_from(points, faces)
    }

    #[test]
    fn cylinder_axis_radius_and_position_are_exact_on_a_strip() {
        let origin = [1.0, -2.0, 3.0];
        let d = oblique_axis();
        for &(radius, steps, arc) in &[
            (7.0, 12, 1.2_f64),
            (0.5, 6, 0.5),   // the small-fillet case: a 0.5 mm radius over ~29°
            (40.0, 24, 2.4), // and a large one
        ] {
            let mesh = cylinder_strip(origin, d, radius, steps, arc);
            let faces: Vec<usize> = (0..mesh.faces.len()).collect();
            let Some(Initial::Cylinder {
                axis_pos,
                axis_dir,
                radius: r,
            }) = cylinder(&faces, &mesh)
            else {
                panic!("no cylinder for r={radius}");
            };
            assert!(
                parallel_miss(axis_dir, d) < 1.0e-14,
                "axis miss {:.3e} for r={radius}",
                parallel_miss(axis_dir, d)
            );
            assert!(
                (r - radius).abs() < 1.0e-9,
                "radius {r} vs {radius} (err {:.3e})",
                (r - radius).abs()
            );
            assert!(
                distance_to_axis(origin, axis_pos, axis_dir) < 1.0e-9,
                "axis position off by {:.3e} for r={radius}",
                distance_to_axis(origin, axis_pos, axis_dir)
            );
        }
    }

    /// The Phase 1.0 selection rule, as a behaviour: a patch that mixes
    /// ruling-aligned quads with triangles straddling three rulings must still
    /// give the exact axis, because selection discards the straddling facets.
    #[test]
    fn cylinder_axis_survives_facets_that_straddle_rulings() {
        let origin = [1.0, -2.0, 3.0];
        let d = oblique_axis();
        let radius = 7.0;
        let mut mesh = cylinder_strip(origin, d, radius, 10, 1.0);

        // Append triangles whose three vertices are on three different rulings
        // AND three different heights — the skew case, which tilts the normal.
        let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);
        let at = |theta: f64, z: f64| {
            [
                origin[0] + radius * (u[0] * theta.cos() + v[0] * theta.sin()) + d[0] * z,
                origin[1] + radius * (u[1] * theta.cos() + v[1] * theta.sin()) + d[1] * z,
                origin[2] + radius * (u[2] * theta.cos() + v[2] * theta.sin()) + d[2] * z,
            ]
        };
        let base = mesh.vertices.len();
        for (theta, z) in [(2.0, 0.0), (2.3, 4.0), (2.6, 1.7)] {
            let p = at(theta, z);
            mesh.vertices.push(MeshVertex::from_xyz(p[0], p[1], p[2]));
        }
        let tri = [base, base + 1, base + 2];
        let mut n = cross3(
            &vsub(at(2.3, 4.0), at(2.0, 0.0)),
            &vsub(at(2.6, 1.7), at(2.0, 0.0)),
        );
        normalize3(&mut n);
        // Sanity: this facet really is skewed, or the test proves nothing.
        assert!(
            dot3(&n, &d).abs() > 1.0e-3,
            "the straddling facet is not actually skewed"
        );
        let mut vertex_indices = [0usize; 4];
        vertex_indices[..3].copy_from_slice(&tri);
        mesh.faces.push(MeshFace {
            vertex_count: 3,
            vertex_indices,
            neighbors: [-1; 4],
            normal: Some(n),
        });

        let faces: Vec<usize> = (0..mesh.faces.len()).collect();
        let Some(Initial::Cylinder { axis_dir, .. }) = cylinder(&faces, &mesh) else {
            panic!("no cylinder");
        };
        assert!(
            parallel_miss(axis_dir, d) < 1.0e-14,
            "straddling facet leaked into the axis: miss {:.3e}",
            parallel_miss(axis_dir, d)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sphere_centre_and_radius_are_exact_from_circumcenter_normal_lines() {
        let centre = [1.0, -2.0, 0.5];
        for &radius in &[6.0_f64, 0.8, 25.0] {
            let d = oblique_axis();
            let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);
            let dir = |a: f64, b: f64| {
                [
                    d[0] * b.cos() + (u[0] * a.cos() + v[0] * a.sin()) * b.sin(),
                    d[1] * b.cos() + (u[1] * a.cos() + v[1] * a.sin()) * b.sin(),
                    d[2] * b.cos() + (u[2] * a.cos() + v[2] * a.sin()) * b.sin(),
                ]
            };
            let on = |a: f64, b: f64| {
                let g = dir(a, b);
                [
                    centre[0] + radius * g[0],
                    centre[1] + radius * g[1],
                    centre[2] + radius * g[2],
                ]
            };
            let mut points = Vec::new();
            let mut faces = Vec::new();
            for k in 0..6 {
                let (a, b) = (k as f64 * 0.6, 0.4 + k as f64 * 0.18);
                let base = points.len();
                points.push(on(a, b));
                points.push(on(a + 0.20, b));
                points.push(on(a, b + 0.17));
                faces.push(vec![base, base + 1, base + 2]);
            }
            let mesh = mesh_from(points, faces);
            let all: Vec<usize> = (0..mesh.faces.len()).collect();

            assert!(
                vnorm(vsub(c, centre)) < 1.0e-9,
                "centre off by {:.3e} for r={radius}",

            );
            assert!(
                (r - radius).abs() < 1.0e-9,
                "radius {r} vs {radius} (err {:.3e})",
                (r - radius).abs()
            );
        }
    }
}

new = '''// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The axis of a surface of revolution, from its normal lines
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The axis line shared by every normal of a surface of revolution, as
/// `(point on the axis, unit direction)`.
///
/// **The bilinear system in the plan is linear in Plücker coordinates.** The
/// meridian-coplanarity constraint `(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = 0` is bilinear in the
/// axis point `a` and direction `d`, which is why the plan proposed alternation
/// or pairwise elimination. Writing the axis as a line rather than as a
/// point-plus-direction removes that entirely. With the line's moment
/// `m = a × d`:
///
/// ```text
///   (pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = d·(pᵢ × nᵢ) − det(a, nᵢ, d)
///                     = d·(pᵢ × nᵢ) + nᵢ·(a × d)
///                     = qᵢ·d + nᵢ·m        where qᵢ = pᵢ × nᵢ
/// ```
///
/// so each facet contributes **one linear equation** in the six unknowns
/// `(d, m)`, and the axis is the null space of the stacked system. No
/// iteration, no alternation, no starting guess. Geometrically the identity is
/// just "every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis", which is
/// why the one solve serves cones and tori alike — and cylinders, though those
/// have a cheaper exact route through `n₁ × n₂`.
///
/// Returns `None` when the null space is not one-dimensional, which is the
/// rank-deficiency the plan warns about: on sphere data every line through the
/// centre satisfies the system, so the null space is three-dimensional and any
/// single answer would be arbitrary.
fn axis_line_from_normals(
    faces: &[usize],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
) -> Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3])> {
    let mut m = nalgebra::Matrix6::<f64>::zeros();
    let mut rows = 0_usize;
    for &fi in faces {
        let Some(n) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else {
            continue;
        };
        let p = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        let q = cross3(&p, &n);
        let row = nalgebra::Vector6::new(q[0], q[1], q[2], n[0], n[1], n[2]);
        m += row * row.transpose();
        rows += 1;
    }
    if rows < 4 {
        return None;
    }

    let eigen = nalgebra::SymmetricEigen::new(m);
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..6).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| eigen.eigenvalues[a].total_cmp(&eigen.eigenvalues[b]));
    let (l0, l1, l5) = (
        eigen.eigenvalues[order[0]],
        eigen.eigenvalues[order[1]],
        eigen.eigenvalues[order[5]],
    );
    // Numerical rank test: the null space must be exactly one-dimensional.
    // Scaled by the largest eigenvalue so it is a relative test on the system's
    // own conditioning rather than an absolute size.
    if !(l5 > 0.0 && l1 * MIN_RANK_GAP > l5 && l0 <= l1) {
        return None;
    }

    let v = eigen.eigenvectors.column(order[0]);
    let mut d = [v[0], v[1], v[2]];
    let scale = normalize3(&mut d);
    if scale < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
        return None;
    }
    // The moment shares the null vector's scale, so divide by the same factor.
    let mut moment = [v[3] / scale, v[4] / scale, v[5] / scale];
    // Enforce the Plücker condition d·m = 0; a nonzero component is numerical
    // drift, not information.
    let drift = dot3(&moment, &d);
    for k in 0..3 {
        moment[k] -= drift * d[k];
    }
    // The point of the axis closest to the origin.
    let point = cross3(&d, &moment);
    Some((point, d))
}

/// Axial and radial coordinates of every patch vertex about `(pos, dir)`.
fn profile_coords(
    faces: &[usize],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    pos: [f64; 3],
    dir: [f64; 3],
) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
    patch_vertices(faces, mesh)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let w = [v.x - pos[0], v.y - pos[1], v.z - pos[2]];
            let z = dot3(&w, &dir);
            let radial = [w[0] - z * dir[0], w[1] - z * dir[1], w[2] - z * dir[2]];
            (dot3(&radial, &radial).sqrt(), z)
        })
        .collect()
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cone
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A cone from its facets: axis from the normal lines, half-angle from the
/// constant `n·d`, apex from where the profile radius reaches zero.
///
/// **This deliberately does not use the normal-covariance axis the plan named**,
/// because that estimator is only correct for narrow cones. The normals of a
/// cone of half-angle α lie on a cone of the same angle about the axis, giving a
/// covariance with eigenvalues `cos²α/2` (twice, perpendicular to the axis) and
/// `sin²α` (along it). The axis is the *smallest* eigenvector only while
/// `sin²α < cos²α/2`, i.e. **α < 35.26°**, and becomes the largest above it.
/// That is not a corner case: a 90° countersink is α = 45°, and the corpus's own
/// `cone_15x20` is α = 36.87°, just past the crossover. The normal-line solve
/// has no such regime — see the test that pins both.
pub(crate) fn cone(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<Initial> {
    let (pos, mut dir) = axis_line_from_normals(faces, mesh)?;

    // n·d is −sin α on every facet; its sign also orients the axis. Averaging
    // costs nothing and is the only place a cone's parameters see more than the
    // minimum support.
    let mut sum = 0.0;
    let mut count = 0_usize;
    for &fi in faces {
        if let Some(n) = mesh.faces[fi].normal {
            sum += dot3(&n, &dir);
            count += 1;
        }
    }
    if count == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mean = sum / count as f64;
    // Orient the axis so that n·d = −sin α with α > 0, i.e. pointing from the
    // apex into the opening.
    if mean > 0.0 {
        dir = [-dir[0], -dir[1], -dir[2]];
    }
    let sin_alpha = mean.abs().min(1.0);
    let half_angle = sin_alpha.asin();
    if !(half_angle.is_finite() && half_angle > 0.0) {
        return None;
    }
    let tan_alpha = half_angle.tan();
    if tan_alpha <= MIN_CROSS_NORM {
        return None;
    }

    // On a cone the profile is the straight line ρ = (z − z_apex)·tan α, so the
    // apex is fixed by the profile's means alone.
    let profile = profile_coords(faces, mesh, pos, dir);
    if profile.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let nf = profile.len() as f64;
    let mean_rho = profile.iter().map(|c| c.0).sum::<f64>() / nf;
    let mean_z = profile.iter().map(|c| c.1).sum::<f64>() / nf;
    let z_apex = mean_z - mean_rho / tan_alpha;
    let apex = [
        pos[0] + dir[0] * z_apex,
        pos[1] + dir[1] * z_apex,
        pos[2] + dir[2] * z_apex,
    ];
    Some(Initial::Cone {
        apex,
        axis_dir: dir,
        half_angle,
    })
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Torus
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A torus from its facets: axis from the normal lines, then `(R, r)` from a
/// circle fit in the `(ρ, z)` profile.
///
/// Phase 1.1 time-boxed this on the suspicion that the axis system would be too
/// ill-conditioned to solve. Phase 1.0 measured its residual on real meshes at
/// **2.354e-5 mm over 23 863 torus facets** — the mesh's own float32 quantum —
/// so the constraint is satisfied to the limit of what the mesh can express, and
/// the Plücker form above removes the conditioning worry that came from
/// alternating on a bilinear system.
pub(crate) fn torus(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<Initial> {
    let (pos, dir) = axis_line_from_normals(faces, mesh)?;
    let profile = profile_coords(faces, mesh, pos, dir);
    if profile.len() < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let ((major, z0), minor) = super::toroidal::fit_circle_2d(&profile)?;
    if !(major > 0.0 && minor > 0.0 && minor < major) {
        return None;
    }
    let centre = [
        pos[0] + dir[0] * z0,
        pos[1] + dir[1] * z0,
        pos[2] + dir[2] * z0,
    ];
    Some(Initial::Torus {
        centre,
        axis_dir: dir,
        major,
        minor,
    })
}

'''

s = s.replace(marker, new + marker, 1)
open(p, "w").write(s)

            let cov_axis = super::super::smallest_eigenvector_3x3(&cov);
            let cov_miss = parallel_miss(cov_axis, d);
            if covariance_should_work {
                assert!(cov_miss < 1.0e-6, "covariance should work at {deg}°: {cov_miss:.3e}");
            } else {
                assert!(
                    cov_miss > 0.5,
                    "covariance should have flipped at {deg}°, miss is only {cov_miss:.3e}"
                );
            }

            // The normal-line solve is right in both regimes.
            let (_, axis) = axis_line_from_normals(&faces, &mesh).unwrap();
            assert!(
                parallel_miss(axis, d) < 1.0e-12,
                "normal-line axis wrong at {deg}°: {:.3e}",
                parallel_miss(axis, d)
            );
        }
    }

    /// A torus patch of quads spanning two meridians and two tube angles. Each
    /// quad is symmetric about its mid-meridian plane, so its Newell normal and
    /// its centroid both lie in that plane — which is exactly the meridian
    /// coplanarity the axis solve relies on.
    fn torus_patch(
        centre: [f64; 3],
        d: [f64; 3],
        major: f64,
        minor: f64,
        n_phi: usize,
        n_psi: usize,
    ) -> ConnectedMesh {
        let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);
        let at = |phi: f64, psi: f64| {
            let mer = [
                u[0] * phi.cos() + v[0] * phi.sin(),
                u[1] * phi.cos() + v[1] * phi.sin(),
                u[2] * phi.cos() + v[2] * phi.sin(),
            ];
            let rad = major + minor * psi.cos();
            [
                centre[0] + rad * mer[0] + minor * psi.sin() * d[0],
                centre[1] + rad * mer[1] + minor * psi.sin() * d[1],
                centre[2] + rad * mer[2] + minor * psi.sin() * d[2],
            ]
        };
        let mut points = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..=n_phi {
            let phi = 0.9 * i as f64 / n_phi as f64;
            for j in 0..=n_psi {
                let psi = 0.4 + 1.3 * j as f64 / n_psi as f64;
                points.push(at(phi, psi));
            }
        }
        let stride = n_psi + 1;
        let mut faces = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..n_phi {
            for j in 0..n_psi {
                faces.push(vec![
                    i * stride + j,
                    (i + 1) * stride + j,
                    (i + 1) * stride + j + 1,
                    i * stride + j + 1,
                ]);
            }
        }
        mesh_from(points, faces)
    }

    #[test]
    fn torus_axis_and_radii_come_out_of_the_meridian_solve() {
        let centre = [1.0, -2.0, 3.0];
        let d = oblique_axis();
        for &(major, minor) in &[(10.0_f64, 2.5_f64), (30.0, 1.0), (4.0, 3.0)] {
            let mesh = torus_patch(centre, d, major, minor, 6, 5);
            let faces: Vec<usize> = (0..mesh.faces.len()).collect();
            let Some(Initial::Torus {
                centre: c,
                axis_dir,
                major: rr,
                minor: r,
            }) = torus(&faces, &mesh)
            else {
                panic!("no torus for R={major} r={minor}");
            };
            assert!(
                parallel_miss(axis_dir, d) < 1.0e-9,
                "axis miss {:.3e} for R={major} r={minor}",
                parallel_miss(axis_dir, d)
            );
            // The centre is only pinned across the axis; along it the torus is
            // symmetric, so compare perpendicular distance to the true axis.
            assert!(
                distance_to_axis(c, centre, d) < 1.0e-6,
                "centre off-axis by {:.3e} for R={major} r={minor}",
                distance_to_axis(c, centre, d)
            );
            assert!(
                (rr - major).abs() < 1.0e-6 && (r - minor).abs() < 1.0e-6,
                "radii ({rr}, {r}) vs ({major}, {minor})"
            );
        }
    }

    /// The rank-deficiency the plan warns about, as a behaviour: on sphere data
    /// every line through the centre satisfies meridian coplanarity, so the
    /// solve must decline rather than invent an axis.
    #[test]
    fn the_axis_solve_declines_on_sphere_data() {
        let centre = [1.0, -2.0, 0.5];
        let radius = 6.0;
        let d = oblique_axis();
        let (u, v) = perpendicular_basis(&d);
        let on = |a: f64, b: f64| {
            [
                centre[0] + radius * (d[0] * b.cos() + (u[0] * a.cos() + v[0] * a.sin()) * b.sin()),
                centre[1] + radius * (d[1] * b.cos() + (u[1] * a.cos() + v[1] * a.sin()) * b.sin()),
                centre[2] + radius * (d[2] * b.cos() + (u[2] * a.cos() + v[2] * a.sin()) * b.sin()),
            ]
        };
        let mut points = Vec::new();
        let mut faces = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..5 {
            for j in 0..5 {
                let (a, b) = (i as f64 * 0.3, 0.4 + j as f64 * 0.25);
                let base = points.len();
                points.push(on(a, b));
                points.push(on(a + 0.28, b));
                points.push(on(a + 0.28, b + 0.24));
                points.push(on(a, b + 0.24));
                faces.push(vec![base, base + 1, base + 2, base + 3]);
            }
        }
        let mesh = mesh_from(points, faces);
        let all: Vec<usize> = (0..mesh.faces.len()).collect();
        assert!(
            axis_line_from_normals(&all, &mesh).is_none(),
            "the solve invented an axis for a sphere"
        );
        assert!(torus(&all, &mesh).is_none());
        // ...while the sphere initializer handles the same patch.
        assert!(matches!(sphere(&all, &mesh), Some(Initial::Sphere { .. })));
    }
'''

The key insight is that the apex is where all rulings converge — it's the unique point that lies on every facet plane. Since each tangent plane along a ruling contains that ruling (which passes through the apex), and each strip quad's plane is a tangent plane containing two rulings, the apex must satisfy all facet plane equations simultaneously. This gives me a linear system: for each facet with normal `n_i` and point `p_i`, I have `n_i · A = n_i · p_i`, where `A` is the apex.

new_cone = '''/// Axis direction and half-angle from the facet normals alone.
///
/// On a cone of half-angle α the normals satisfy `nᵢ·d = −sin α` — one linear
/// equation per facet in the four unknowns `(d, sin α)` — so the answer is the
/// null space of the stacked `[nᵢ | 1]`. It needs only normals, never positions,
/// which is what makes it work on the single ring of facets a real cone
/// tessellation actually has.
fn cone_direction_and_angle(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<([f64; 3], f64)> {
    let mut m = nalgebra::Matrix4::<f64>::zeros();
    let mut rows = 0_usize;
    for &fi in faces {
        let Some(n) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else {
            continue;
        };
        let row = nalgebra::Vector4::new(n[0], n[1], n[2], 1.0);
        m += row * row.transpose();
        rows += 1;
    }
    if rows < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let eigen = nalgebra::SymmetricEigen::new(m);
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..4).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| eigen.eigenvalues[a].total_cmp(&eigen.eigenvalues[b]));
    let (l1, l3) = (eigen.eigenvalues[order[1]], eigen.eigenvalues[order[3]]);
    if !(l3 > 0.0 && l1 * MIN_RANK_GAP > l3) {
        return None; // the null space is not one-dimensional
    }

    let v = eigen.eigenvectors.column(order[0]);
    let mut d = [v[0], v[1], v[2]];
    let dnorm = normalize3(&mut d);
    if dnorm < MIN_CROSS_NORM {
        return None;
    }
    let mut sin_alpha = v[3] / dnorm;
    // The null vector's overall sign is free; fix it so sin α > 0, which also
    // orients the axis from the apex into the opening.
    if sin_alpha < 0.0 {
        sin_alpha = -sin_alpha;
        d = [-d[0], -d[1], -d[2]];
    }
    if !(sin_alpha > 0.0 && sin_alpha < 1.0) {
        return None; // a cylinder (α = 0) or a degenerate solve
    }
    Some((d, sin_alpha.asin()))
}

/// A cone from its facets: the apex from where their planes concur, the
/// direction and half-angle from the normals.
///
/// **Neither of the two routes the plan and the module's own torus solve use
/// would work here**, and the reason is worth recording:
///
/// * The *normal-covariance* axis the plan named is not the axis in general.
///   A cone's normals lie on a cone of the same half-angle about the axis, and
///   over a full revolution the covariance has eigenvalues `cos²α/2` twice and
///   `sin²α` once, so the axis is the smallest eigenvector only while
///   **α < 35.26°** — a 90° countersink is 45°, and the corpus's `cone_15x20`
///   is 36.87°. Over the partial arc an earned patch actually has, the
///   perpendicular spread is not even isotropic and the estimator degrades
///   further. The test pins both regimes.
/// * The *normal-line concurrence* solve used for the torus is
///   **rank-deficient on a single ring of cone facets**, which is exactly what
///   a real cone tessellation is: a cone is ruled, so one row of quads spans
///   its whole height, every facet centroid sits at the same axial position,
///   and their normal lines then all meet the axis at the *same* point. Any
///   line through that point satisfies the system, so the axis is not
///   determined. (On a torus the meeting point slides with the tube angle,
///   which is why the same solve is well posed there.)
///
/// What does work is exact and needs no arc at all: **a cone's tangent plane
/// along a ruling contains that ruling, and every ruling passes through the
/// apex, so every facet plane contains the apex.** That is one linear equation
/// per facet, `nᵢ·A = nᵢ·pᵢ`, and three independent normals pin `A` exactly.
pub(crate) fn cone(faces: &[usize], mesh: &ConnectedMesh) -> Option<Initial> {
    let (axis_dir, half_angle) = cone_direction_and_angle(faces, mesh)?;

    // The apex is the common point of the facet planes.
    let mut m = nalgebra::Matrix3::<f64>::zeros();
    let mut b = nalgebra::Vector3::<f64>::zeros();
    for &fi in faces {
        let Some(n) = mesh.faces[fi].normal else {
            continue;
        };
        let p = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        let row = nalgebra::Vector3::new(n[0], n[1], n[2]);
        m += row * row.transpose();
        b += row * dot3(&n, &p);
    }
    let eigen = nalgebra::SymmetricEigen::new(m);
    let mut evs: Vec<f64> = eigen.eigenvalues.iter().copied().collect();
    evs.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    // The planes must span all three directions, or their intersection is a
    // line or a plane rather than a point.
    if !(evs[2] > 0.0 && evs[0] * MIN_RANK_GAP > evs[2]) {
        return None;
    }
    let apex_v = m.lu().solve(&b)?;
    let apex = [apex_v[0], apex_v[1], apex_v[2]];

    Some(Initial::Cone {
        apex,
        axis_dir,
        half_angle,
    })
}

'''

///   Measured on a 10-step, 1.1 rad strip at α = 10°: Δθ = 0.11 rad predicts

/// The sign is deliberately not resolved here; [`cone`] orients the axis

/// winding.
fn cone_direction_and_angle(
    apex: [f64; 3],
    faces: &[usize],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
) -> Option<([f64; 3], f64)> {
    let mut m = nalgebra::Matrix4::<f64>::zeros();
    let mut rows = 0_usize;
    for vi in patch_vertices(faces, mesh) {

            continue; // a vertex at the apex says nothing about the axis

        m += row * row.transpose();
        rows += 1;
    }
    if rows < 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let eigen = nalgebra::SymmetricEigen::new(m);
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..4).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| eigen.eigenvalues[a].total_cmp(&eigen.eigenvalues[b]));
    let (l1, l3) = (eigen.eigenvalues[order[1]], eigen.eigenvalues[order[3]]);

        return None; // the null space is not one-dimensional
    }

    let v = eigen.eigenvectors.column(order[0]);

    let mut evs: Vec<f64> = eigen.eigenvalues.iter().copied().collect();
    evs.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    // The planes must span all three directions, or their intersection is a
    // line or a plane rather than a point.
    if !(evs[2] > 0.0 && evs[0] > evs[2] * MIN_NULLSPACE_SEPARATION) {
        return None;
    }
    let apex_v = m.lu().solve(&b)?;
    let apex = [apex_v[0], apex_v[1], apex_v[2]];

    let (mut axis_dir, half_angle) = cone_direction_and_angle(apex, faces, mesh)?;

    // Orient the axis from the apex toward the support — geometric, so it does
    // not inherit the mesh's normal convention.
    let mut toward = [0.0_f64; 3];
    for &fi in faces {
        let p = face_centroid(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices);
        for k in 0..3 {
            toward[k] += p[k] - apex[k];
        }
    }
    if dot3(&toward, &axis_dir) < 0.0 {
        axis_dir = [-axis_dir[0], -axis_dir[1], -axis_dir[2]];
    }

    Some(Initial::Cone {
        apex,
        axis_dir,
        half_angle,
    })
}

/// \`p(θ, z) = a + r(cos θ · u + sin θ · v) + z · d\`. The facet's plane contains
/// the direction \`d\` — equivalently \`n ⟂ d\` — iff the vertices, projected along
/// \`d\` onto the plane perpendicular to it, are collinear. They land on a circle
/// of radius \`r\`, and three points on a circle are collinear only when two of
/// them coincide. **So \`n ⟂ d\` exactly when two vertices share a ruling**, and a
/// triangle straddling three distinct rulings tilts its normal off
/// perpendicular however perfect the underlying cylinder is.
fn min_ruling_gap_rad(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, axis_pos: [f64; 3], axis: [f64; 3]) -> Option<f64> {
    let d = unit(axis)?;
    let seed = if d[0].abs() < 0.9 { [1.0, 0.0, 0.0] } else { [0.0, 1.0, 0.0] };

...

/// exporter's angular step (≥1e-2 rad). Any cut in that gap gives the same
/// split. The gap is reported beside the split so a mesh that lands inside it

const RULING_SAME_RAD: f64 = 1.0e-6;

All four initializers are exact on synthetic data (numbers in TODO.md 1.1), but
three of the four constructions the Phase 1 design named turned out to be wrong,
and the reasons generalize past this step.

**The bilinear system was an artefact of the coordinates.** The design records
the torus axis constraint `(pᵢ − a)·(nᵢ × d) = 0` as bilinear in the axis point
and direction, to be solved "by alternation or pairwise elimination". Writing the
axis as a *line* rather than a point-plus-direction removes the bilinearity
outright: with the moment `m = a × d`, the constraint becomes `qᵢ·d + nᵢ·m = 0`
where `qᵢ = pᵢ × nᵢ` — one linear equation per facet in six unknowns, solved as a
null space with no iteration and no starting guess. The identity underneath is
"every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". The one caveat is
scaling: the `q` block carries length units and the `n` block does not, so the
system must be normalized to the patch's own centroid and extent first or the
null space is lost in the scale mismatch rather than in the data.

**A cone is not a surface of revolution as far as this solve is concerned.** The
same normal-line construction is *rank-deficient on a single ring of cone
facets*, and a single ring is exactly what a real cone tessellation is: a cone is
ruled, so one row of quads spans its entire height, every facet centroid sits at
the same axial position, and their normal lines then all meet the axis at the
same point. Any line through that point satisfies the system. On a torus the
meeting point slides with the tube angle, which is why the identical solve is
well posed there. The lesson is that "surface of revolution" is not the property
that makes the solve work — *variation in where the normal lines cross the axis*
is.

**The normal-covariance cone axis has a regime the plan did not account for.**
A cone's normals lie on a cone of the same half-angle about the axis, so over a
full revolution the covariance has eigenvalues `cos²α/2` (twice) and `sin²α`
(once), and the axis is the smallest eigenvector only while **α < 35.26°**. That
is not exotic: a 90° countersink is 45°, and the corpus's own `cone_15x20` is
36.87°. Over the partial arc an earned patch actually has, the perpendicular
spread is not isotropic either and it degrades before that. What replaces it is
both exact and arc-free: **every facet plane of a cone contains the apex**,
because a tangent plane along a ruling contains that ruling and all rulings meet
at the apex — and this holds for the chord plane of a strip quad too, since two
rulings still meet there. So `nᵢ·A = nᵢ·pᵢ` pins the apex from three independent
normals, whatever the tessellation, and direction and half-angle follow from the
vertex directions about it.

**Facet normals are exact for directions and biased for angles.** The
perpendicularity result from Phase 1.0 says a ruling-aligned facet normal is
*exactly* perpendicular to the axis. It does not say the normal equals the
tangent-plane normal: a strip quad's chord plane leans off it by
`n·d = sin α·cos(Δθ/2)/√(1 − sin²α sin²(Δθ/2))`, an `O(Δθ²/8)` bias. Predicted
1.5e-3 relative at Δθ = 0.11 rad, and the half-angle measured 9.985° against a
true 10.000° — the same 1.5e-3. Vertices carry no such bias because they lie on
the surface exactly, so wherever a quantity can be taken from vertices rather
than from normals, it should be.

**The conditioning floor is not a model selector, and the attempt to make it one
was the familiar trap.** The meridian system is rank-deficient by construction on
sphere data, so it was tempting to threshold the spectrum tightly enough to
reject a sphere. Measured, the separation is not available: the degenerate sphere
patch reads `l1/l5` = 2.06e-6 and the hardest genuine torus (R = 4, r = 3) reads
9.2e-4, a factor of 450 with nothing but data-dependence between them — TODO
rule 5's "detector needs just one threshold" reached from yet another direction.
The floor stayed purely numerical, and *structure* does the discrimination for
free: a sphere's (ρ, z) profile is a circle centred on the axis, so its fitted
major radius comes out ~0 and the `minor < major` check rejects it outright. This
is what the design meant by "ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede
it" — type discrimination belongs to the ladder and to validation, never to a
conditioning guard.

### Phase 2 design: distance-guided exploration"""
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, new, 1)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print("ok")

## All four initializers are exact

[src/stage2/initialize.rs](src/stage2/initialize.rs), 8 unit tests, deliberately **not wired in** — 1.2's earn loop is what calls them. Measured on synthetic data, well inside the step's ~1e-9 bar:

| initializer | accuracy |
|---|---|
| cylinder | axis 1e-14, radius 1e-9, position 1e-9 (r = 0.5, 7, 40) |
| sphere | centre and radius 1e-9 |
| cone | axis 2.8e-14–1.9e-12, half-angle 1.5e-12°–1.0e-10°, apex 3e-14–5e-13 mm (10°–75°) |
| torus | axis 1e-9, centre 1e-6, radii 1e-6 (r/R = 0.25, 0.033, 0.75) |

The torus is no longer a risk — consistent with 1.0's prediction from its residual at the mesh quantum.

## Three of the four constructions the plan named were wrong

Each replaced on a measurement, and each of the *wrong* ones is the intuitive one:

1. **The "bilinear" meridian system is linear.** In Plücker coordinates, with the moment `m = a × d`, the constraint becomes `q·d + n·m = 0` — one linear equation per facet, no alternation, no starting guess. Underneath it's just "every normal line of a surface of revolution meets the axis". It does need normalizing to the patch centroid and extent first, or the length-carrying `q` block and the dimensionless `n` block differ by orders of magnitude and the null space drowns in the scale mismatch. (That bit me as a real bug first.)

2. **A cone can't use that solve at all** — and the failing case is the normal one. A cone is ruled, so one row of quads spans its whole height, every facet centroid sits at the same axial position, and the normal lines then all meet the axis at the *same point*; any line through that point solves the system. A torus is fine only because the meeting point slides with the tube angle. So "surface of revolution" isn't the enabling property — *variation in where the normal lines cross the axis* is.

3. **The normal-covariance cone axis flips at α = 35.26°** (eigenvalues `cos²α/2` twice, `sin²α` once). A 90° countersink is 45°; the corpus's own `cone_15x20` is 36.87°, already past it. What replaces it is exact and needs no arc: **every facet plane of a cone contains the apex**, including a strip quad's chord plane, so `n·A = n·p` pins the apex from three normals.

4. A fourth correction that sharpens 1.0: a ruling-aligned facet normal is exactly perpendicular to the axis, but it is **not** the tangent-plane normal. A chord plane leans by `O(Δθ²/8)` — predicted 1.5e-3 relative at Δθ = 0.11 rad, measured 9.985° against 10.000°, the same 1.5e-3. The half-angle now comes from vertices, which lie on the surface exactly.

## One place I stopped rather than tuned

I tried to make the rank floor sharp enough to reject sphere data, since the meridian system is rank-deficient there by construction. The separation isn't available: the degenerate sphere reads `l1/l5` = 2.06e-6 against 9.2e-4 for the hardest genuine torus — a factor of 450 with nothing but data-dependence in between, which is rule 5's "detector needs just one threshold" from a new direction. So the floor stayed purely numerical, and **structure discriminates for free**: a sphere's (ρ, z) profile is a circle centred on the axis, so its major radius fits to ~0 and `minor < major` rejects it. That's what the plan meant by "ladder order and a conditioning floor must precede it".

Selection is part of the algorithm now, per 1.0: widest normal pair, then re-picked among facets ruling-aligned to that provisional axis. A test mixes aligned quads with a straddling triangle and demands the exact axis anyway. `min_ruling_gap_rad` and `RULING_SAME_RAD` moved into this module and `reference.rs` imports them, so the instrument and the code acting on its findings can't drift apart.

**Next is 1.2**, the earn loop — which is what consumes these and lets the module's `allow(dead_code)` come off.

//! Stage 2.3(b): scoped fit competition.
//!
//! For a smooth region the whole-region ladder (2.3(a)) cannot explain — a
//! tangent chain like the rounded-cube shell (6 planes, 12 fillet cylinders,
//! 8 corner spheres) or the nosecone's cone+sphere — decompose it by
//! seed-first multi-type competition run INSIDE the region. The sharp
//! boundary cordons the arena, so competition cost is bounded and
//! cross-region accidents are impossible.
//!
//! - **Seeds**: every region face seeds exactly once, in jet-interior-first
//!   order (faces whose (κ1,κ2) best match their neighbors' seed before
//!   junction rows). Committing a hypothesis does NOT retire the faces it grew
//!   into — growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion, and a face
//!   swallowed by a wrong surface must still be able to seed the right one
//!   (\`resolve_claims\` arbitrates the resulting multi-claims). Only faces in
//!   the *interior* of the explained set are skipped, since a fit grown from
//!   the middle of a validated surface merely refits that surface.
//! - **Per seed**: grow each candidate surface type (jet-pruned) from a
//!   small jet-similar seed patch — fit, flood-accept every region face the
//!   fit validates, refit on the grown support, to a fixpoint — and commit
//!   the hypothesis with the **largest validated area** (simplest-DOF
//!   tiebreak). The jet only orders and prunes; vertex-tolerance validation
//!   decides every face.
//! - **Claims**: a flood may grow through faces already claimed by an
//!   earlier hypothesis (junction rows that genuinely lie on two surfaces),
//!   so a face can be claimed by several hypotheses. \`resolve_claims\`
//!   assigns each contested face to the claimant that fits its vertices best
//!   (2× margin to leave the larger claimant).
//! - **Toroidal candidates (stage 2.3(c))**: a torus competes like any other
//!   type — grown directly from curved seeds (fillet tori, bend tubes), and
//!   additionally *promoted* from a cylinder whose flood stalled against
//!   faces whose jet continues the tube (κ1 ≈ the tube's 1/r, |κ2| well

//!

fn grow<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
    grow_from::<S>(mesh, in_region, seed, patch, centroids, config, min_faces)
}

/// The grow loop proper, from an explicit initial fit patch and flood start:
/// fit the patch, flood-accept every region face the fit validates, refit on
/// the grown support, to a fixpoint. Returns the hypothesis, its validated
/// area, and its face list.
fn grow_from<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    start: usize,
    initial: Vec<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let mut accepted =
        condition_patch::<S>(mesh, start, initial, centroids, config, vtol, stol, min_faces);
    let mut prev = 0usize;
    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
        let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
        if comp.is_empty() {
            return None; // the start face does not lie on its own fit — reject
        }
        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
            accepted = comp;
            break;
        }
        if comp.len() == prev {
            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
                accepted = comp;
            }
            break;
        }
        prev = accepted.len();
        accepted = comp;
    }

    // Final fit + validated flood.
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &accepted);
    let mut fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, &accepted, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
    S::determine_convexity(mesh, &accepted, &mut fit);
    let faces = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
    if faces.len() < min_faces {
        return None;
    }
    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
    Some((hyp, area, faces))
}

fn flood<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    fit: &S::Fit,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
) -> Vec<usize> {
    if !face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
    seen.insert(seed);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut stack = vec![seed];
    while let Some(fi) = stack.pop() {
        out.push(fi);
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            if in_region[ni]
                && !seen.contains(&ni)
                && face_validates::<S>(mesh, ni, fit, centroids, vtol, stol)
            {
                seen.insert(ni);
                stack.push(ni);
            }
        }
    }
    out.sort_unstable();
    out
}

/// Does face \`fi\` validate \`fit\` (all vertices ≤ vtol, centroid ≤ stol,
/// orientation coherent)?
fn face_validates<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    fi: usize,
    fit: &S::Fit,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
) -> bool {
    if !S::convexity_check(fit, mesh, fi) {
        return false;
    }
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
    for &vi in &face.vertex_indices[..vc] {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
        if S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z]) > vtol {
            return false;
        }
    }
    S::centroid_distance(fit, &centroids[fi]) <= stol
}

/// Max distance from any vertex of face \`fi\` to \`fit\` — the trim criterion for
/// conditioning the seed patch (\`condition_patch\`).
fn face_max_vertex_dist<S: SurfaceType>(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, fi: usize, fit: &S::Fit) -> f64 {
    let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
    let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
    face.vertex_indices[..vc]
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            S::vertex_distance(fit, &[v.x, v.y, v.z])
        })
        .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max)
}

> I'm seeing how `grow` orchestrates the process: it calls `seed_patch` followed by `grow_from`, which then runs `condition_patch` and iterates through fit, flood, and refit cycles. The key insight for Phase 1.2 is that instead of these blind patching steps, `grow` should generate an earned patch through a loop that validates patches before using them.
> 
> The earn loop itself is a BFS from the seed that admits frontier faces only if they pass validation at the current fit tolerance, attempting promotions up the type ladder (plane → cylinder/cone → sphere → torus) when validation fails, and excluding faces that can't validate at any level. But here's the design tension: `grow` is generic over a single SurfaceType, yet the earn loop with promotion crosses types—so I need to figure out whether the earn loop replaces the per-type competition entirely or sits inside each type's individual `grow` call.
> 
> Looking at the plan more carefully, the earn loop produces multiple (type, patch, params) tuples that each get handed to `grow_from` for their respective type. That means the earn loop itself can't be generic over S—it needs to work with a dynamic type ladder and run once per seed, not once per seed per type. So `compete_region` needs significant restructuring: call the earn loop once, then dispatch each result into the appropriate `grow_from::<S>`.

pub(super) fn compete_region(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
    for &fi in &region.faces {
        in_region[fi] = true;
    }

    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };

    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
        .map(|fi| {
            if !in_region[fi] {
                return f64::INFINITY;
            }
            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
        })
        .collect();
    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
        score[a]
            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
            .unwrap()
            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
    });

    // Every region face seeds exactly once — \`seeds\` is a permutation of them,
    // which is what terminates the loop. Committing a hypothesis does NOT
    // remove the faces it grew into from the seed pool.
    //
    // Growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. The committed
    // face set is always a \`flood\` output, so every member validates — but
    // against a fit whose parameters came from an unvalidated seed
    // neighbourhood, so "validated" does not mean "the right surface". Letting
    // those faces seed too means a wrong hypothesis can be out-competed by a
    // right one grown from a face it had swallowed; \`resolve_claims\` already
    // exists to arbitrate the multi-claims that produces.
    //
    // It also makes the long-standing claim that seed misordering "costs only
    // time" actually true: previously an early bad hypothesis consumed faces a
    // later, better seed needed.
    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();
    let mut claim_lists: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n]; // face -> committed idxs
    let mut claimed = vec![false; n];

    for &seed in &seeds {
        // Skip only faces in the INTERIOR of what is already explained: every
        // neighbour claimed too. Seeding there cannot produce a competitor —
        // a fit grown from the middle of a validated surface refits that same
        // surface — so it is pure cost. Faces at the margin still seed.
        if claimed[seed] && interior_of_claims(mesh, seed, &claimed) {
            continue;
        }
        let jf = jet[seed];
        // Dominant / secondary principal-curvature MAGNITUDES. The jet orders
        // k1 ≥ k2 by signed value, so for a concave feature (a hole wall,
        // κ = −1/r) the dominant curvature is negative and lands in k2 —
        // taking |k1| as the dominant would read the wall's flat axial
        // direction and treat the hole as planar. Order by magnitude instead.
        let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
        let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());

        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
                let sweep = candidate_sweep(mesh, &h);
                if sweep < MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG.to_radians() {
                    if debug {
                        eprintln!(
                            "    compete: seed {seed} rejected {} sweeping only {:.1}\u{00b0} about its axis — radius undetermined ({} faces, area {area:.2})",
                            h.kind_name(),
                            sweep.to_degrees(),
                            h.faces().len(),
                        );
                    }
                    return;
                }
                let better = match best {
                    None => true,
                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
                };
                if better {
                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
                }
            }
        };

        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
        let mut cone_area = None;
        let mut sphere_area = None;
        let mut torus_area = None;
        if a1 >= flat_eps {
            // Curved: a developable (cylinder/cone) is always plausible.
            let cone = grow::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES);
            cone_area = cone.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

            // Toroidal candidate: a direct grow from this seed (fillet tori,
            // bend tubes), skipped when the seed reads sphere-like — every
            // adjacent quad-row band of a sphere lies near some torus, so a
            // (κ,κ) seed's torus is at best a bogus band that loses to the
            // sphere anyway. A torus seed reads |κ2| < |κ1| (κ2 varies
            // azimuthally around the tube; it only approaches κ1 near the
            // degenerate R≈r hole of a donut — a whole-region ladder case,
            // not a competition case).
            let mut torus = if a2 < 0.8 * a1 {
                let patch = seed_patch(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet);
                torus_candidate(mesh, &in_region, &patch, &[seed], centroids, config)
            } else {
                None
            };
            // Bent-tube promotion: a cylinder that stalled against
            // tube-continuation faces is the developable prefix of a bent
            // tube; grow a torus from the pure-bend patch past the stall.
            if let Some((cyl, _, cyl_faces)) = cone.as_ref() {
                if cyl.is_cylinder() {
                    let promoted =
                        promote_bend(mesh, &in_region, cyl, cyl_faces, jet, centroids, config);
                    if let Some(p) = promoted {
                        if torus.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, a, _)| p.1 > *a) {
                            torus = Some(p);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            torus_area = torus.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

            consider(cone.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Conical(h), a)), 2, &mut best);
            // Curved in both directions → also try a sphere.
            if a2 >= 0.3 * a1 {
                let sphere = grow::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES);
                sphere_area = sphere.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
                consider(sphere.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Spherical(h), a)), 1, &mut best);
            }
            consider(torus.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h), a)), 3, &mut best);
        }
        let plane_area = plane.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
        consider(plane.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Planar(h), a)), 0, &mut best);

        if debug && best.is_none() {
            eprintln!(
                "    compete: seed {seed} jet=({:.3},{:.3}) class {:?} → NO GROWTH (plane {plane_area:?} cone {cone_area:?} sphere {sphere_area:?} torus {torus_area:?})",
                jf.k1, jf.k2, curvature_class(jf),
            );
        }

        if let Some((hyp, area, dof)) = best {
            if debug {
                eprintln!(
                    "    compete: seed {seed} → {} ({} faces, area {area:.2}, dof {dof}, sweep {:.1}\u{00b0})",
                    hyp.kind_name(),
                    hyp.faces().len(),
                    match &hyp {
                        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(t) => torus_sweep(mesh, t).to_degrees(),
                        CompeteHyp::Conical(c) => conical_sweep(mesh, c).to_degrees(),
                        _ => 0.0,
                    }
                );
            }
            let idx = committed.len();
            for &f in hyp.faces() {
                claim_lists[f].push(idx);
                claimed[f] = true;
            }
            committed.push(hyp);
        }
        // A seed that grows nothing analytic costs only its own turn.
    }

    resolve_claims(
        mesh,
        &region.faces,
        &mut committed,
        &claim_lists,
        config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
        config,
    )
}

/// explained set and cannot seed anything new.

/// A face that validates no rung is not a failure — it is the patch's seam
/// boundary, discovered rather than detected. Tangent junctions cannot be found
/// by curvature (measured dead twice; a tangent junction is locally the
/// smoothest place on the mesh), but they fall out of a fit that stops
/// explaining the next face. Those faces are counted here and are what Phase 2
/// consumes as distance-field sources.
fn earn_patch(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> (Vec<usize>, EarnStats) {
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let mut stats = EarnStats::default();

    let mut accepted = vec![seed];
    let Some(mut rung) = fit_rung(0, mesh, &accepted) else {
        stats.final_rung = "none";
        return (accepted, stats);
    };
    let mut kind = 0_usize;
    let mut last_refit = 1_usize;

    let mut seen: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
    seen.insert(seed);
    let mut queue: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let push_neighbours = |queue: &mut Vec<usize>, seen: &mut HashSet<usize>, fi: usize| {
        let vc = mesh.faces[fi].vertex_count as usize;
        for &ni in &mesh.faces[fi].neighbors[..vc] {
            if ni < 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let ni = ni as usize;
            if in_region[ni] && seen.insert(ni) {
                queue.push(ni);
            }
        }
    };
    push_neighbours(&mut queue, &mut seen, seed);

    while let Some(cand) = queue.pop() {
        if rung.validates(mesh, cand, centroids, vtol, stol) {
            accepted.push(cand);
            push_neighbours(&mut queue, &mut seen, cand);
            // Refit on doubling; the current fit stays valid for what it has
            // already admitted either way.
            if accepted.len() >= last_refit * EARN_REFIT_GROWTH {
                if let Some(r) = fit_rung(kind, mesh, &accepted) {
                    rung = r;
                }
                last_refit = accepted.len();
            }
            continue;
        }

        // The face does not validate. Try climbing the ladder: a higher rung
        // may explain the whole patch INCLUDING this face. Requiring every
        // already-accepted face to validate under the promoted fit is what
        // stops a promotion from quietly swapping in a surface that explains
        // the frontier at the cost of the patch.
        stats.promotions_attempted += 1;
        let mut trial = accepted.clone();
        trial.push(cand);
        let mut promoted = false;
        for next in (kind + 1)..=4 {
            let Some(r) = fit_rung(next, mesh, &trial) else {
                continue;
            };
            if trial
                .iter()
                .all(|&fi| r.validates(mesh, fi, centroids, vtol, stol))
            {
                rung = r;
                kind = next;
                accepted = trial;
                last_refit = accepted.len();
                push_neighbours(&mut queue, &mut seen, cand);
                stats.promotions_accepted += 1;
                promoted = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if !promoted {
            // Across a seam. Excluded, and recorded.
            stats.frontier_faces += 1;
        }
    }

    // One final refit, then drop anything it no longer explains, so the patch
    // that leaves here validates a single fit rather than a history of them.
    if let Some(r) = fit_rung(kind, mesh, &accepted) {
        let kept: Vec<usize> = accepted
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&fi| r.validates(mesh, fi, centroids, vtol, stol))
            .collect();
        if !kept.is_empty() && kept.contains(&seed) {
            accepted = kept;
            rung = r;
        }
    }
    stats.final_rung = rung.name();
    accepted.sort_unstable();
    accepted.dedup();
    (accepted, stats)
}

''' + anchor

> On a fine mesh where the sag is below tolerance, the plane would actually validate and grow across the whole cylinder as a large "planar" patch, which then gets passed to other surface types. ```markdown
# Phase 1.2 earn loop — design correction to apply after the baseline finishes

## The flaw in the first cut

I wrote `earn_patch` as **type-agnostic**: one patch per seed, climbing a single
global ladder, handed to every type the competition tries. That is wrong, and
the plan's "branch on ambiguity" bullet is the symptom.

Concretely: a seed on a sphere. Two adjacent facets of a sphere also validate a
*cylinder* (the hole→sphere trap in reverse). The ladder climbs to cylinder,
grows a band around the sphere, and stops where the cylinder stops explaining.
`grow::<SphericalSurface>` then receives a band-shaped patch — and a sphere
fitted to a band is exactly the under-determined case `MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG`
exists to reject. The earned patch would have *created* the ambiguity the plan
then proposes to branch out of.

## The fix: make the earn loop type-directed

`earn_patch::<S>` grows the patch under **S's own** fit, bootstrapping through
the lower rungs only far enough to determine S. The outer competition already
enumerates the four types per seed, so each type earns its own patch and the
ambiguity never arises — no branching needed, and no second model-selection
mechanism competing with the one that already exists.

This also keeps the change a true drop-in for `seed_patch`, which is what the
step asks for: `grow<S>` is already generic over S.

## Ladders (rung codes 0=plane 1=cylinder 2=sphere 3=cone 4=torus)

| type | ladder | why |
|---|---|---|
| PlanarSurface | [0] | a plane is determined by one facet |
| SphericalSurface | [0, 2] | two facets' circumcenter normal lines give the centre |
| ConicalSurface | [0, 1, 3] | plane → cylinder (2 normals) → cone (needs 3+) |
| ToroidalSurface | [0, 1, 4] | plane → cylinder → torus (needs 4+ for the axis) |

Matches the plan's "plane → cylinder/cone or sphere → torus" exactly.

Add to the `SurfaceType` trait:

    /// Rungs this type's earned patch climbs, in order, ending at the type
    /// itself — see `compete::earn_patch`.
    const EARN_LADDER: &'static [u8];

## Other corrections to fold in

1. **BFS, not DFS.** `queue.pop()` on a `Vec` is LIFO; the step says BFS and a
   BFS patch stays local and round, which is what conditioning wants. Use
   `VecDeque::pop_front`.
2. Keep the doubling refit + final refit-and-filter pass, so the returned patch
   validates one single fit.
3. Keep the excluded-face count: those are the seam frontier Phase 2 consumes.

```
